attempts.summary: Built an Ansible playbook (run from node2, the only node with ansible installed) that creates an SSH host certificate authority on node1 (/etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca), signs node1's ed25519 host public key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with principals node1,10.100.12.10, configures sshd to present that certificate via HostCertificate/HostKey directives, validates config, and restarts sshd. A bootstrap step (ssh-keygen -A + starting the inactive ssh.service, which had no host keys at all on this baseline image) was needed before Ansible/SSH could reach node1 at all. Verified end-to-end: on node2 (the client), removed any pinned host-key known_hosts entries and added only a `@cert-authority node1,10.100.12.10 <CA-pubkey>` trust line, then connected with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes and confirmed via verbose SSH output that the client validated node1 purely via the CA certificate ("Host is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate"), with no pinned key needed. Then ran the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot-id + service/config baselines on both nodes, restarted node1 (boot_id bdd5de93→b878380d) and confirmed sshd, CA files, and cert-based trust all survived; restarted node2 (boot_id eefaca89→f6406f97) and confirmed the Ansible artifacts, SSH client keys, and CA-trusted connection to node1 still worked afterward.
